index.title: Ship identity faster with production-ready SDKs and API clients.
index.lead: Autional gives your team a unified package surface for authentication, MFA, tenants, passkeys, sessions, and policy-heavy enterprise flows without stitching together multiple vendors.

meta.title: Quickstart — Autional Developers
meta.description: Add Autional authentication to your app — AI-assisted quickstart: boot the platform, hand the integration prompt to your assistant, and verify against the live API.

quickstart.title: Add authentication to an existing app in one guided run.
quickstart.lead: This quickstart is built for teams using AI-assisted integration: start the Autional stack, hand the structured integration prompt to your assistant, then verify the result against live APIs rather than mock flows.

items: A running Autional environment (self-hosted: start locally with Docker; cloud hosting is on the roadmap).
Your application source code ready for SDK integration.
An AI coding assistant such as Cursor, Claude Code, or another capable LLM.
prereq.note: A standard SaaS application usually reaches a first working integration in about 30 minutes when the assistant can inspect the real codebase.

steps.title: Move from blank integration to verified auth flow.

items.title: Boot the platform
items.copy: Start the local Autional stack so the assistant can register tenants, inspect APIs, and verify the final flow against a real environment.

items.title: Give the assistant the integration prompt
items.copy: Hand the assistant a structured prompt so it can analyze the project, pick the right SDK package, and land a verifiable integration.

items.title: Review and validate
items.copy: Once the code is generated, verify tenant registration, proxy rules, and end-to-end auth behavior before rolling the change out to your team.

items: Authentication flows: login, registration, logout, token refresh, and profile retrieval.
Security defaults: SHA-256 password transmission, JWT verification, and tenant-aware flows.
Operational setup: proxy guidance that avoids cross-origin issues during local development.
Project hygiene: integration notes your team can keep after the AI finishes the first pass.

rows.resolution: Check that the request path includes the /tenant/ segment, for example /bff/tenant/api/v1/tenant/public/tenants.
Use SHA-256(rawPassword + "|" + tenantId) when testing the login payload.
Configure framework rewrites or a development proxy instead of calling the gateway directly from the browser.
Add "downlevelIteration": true to tsconfig.json if your target tooling requires it.
Set appId to any non-empty identifier such as the current project name.

meta.title: Migration Guide — Autional Developers
meta.description: Migrate from Auth0, Clerk, Firebase Auth, or Keycloak to Autional. Cut-over playbooks with step-by-step instructions.

migration.title: Cut over from your current auth stack without losing control.
migration.lead: These playbooks cover the key migration work: tenant setup, user export and import, SDK replacement, policy mapping, and final verification; ground each step with the docs site and the API reference.

auth0.title: From Auth0
steps: Create an Autional tenant → configure Auth0 as IdP
Export Auth0 rules → rebuild with Autional RBAC roles and policies
Update the SDK from auth0-js to @autional/react
Verify token validation with the Autional JWKS endpoint

clerk.title: From Clerk
steps: Export users via the Clerk API → import into an Autional tenant
Update webhook endpoints to the Autional event format
Verify SSO + MFA configuration on the Autional admin console

firebase.title: From Firebase Auth
steps: Export users from Firebase → import via the Autional admin API
Migrate custom claims to Autional RBAC roles
Reconfigure social login providers in Autional

keycloak.title: From Keycloak
steps: Export the Keycloak realm → Autional tenant config
Synchronize users via the SCIM 2.0 protocol
Map Keycloak roles to Autional RBAC

bottom.title: Ready to migrate?
bottom.lead: See the quickstart for onboarding, the docs site for platform deployment and application docs, and the API reference for endpoint details.
